title: New Tractor Plant Bringing 50 Jobs and $10.5 Million Investment to Monroeville - NewsBreak
text:
3 hours ago Governor Kay Ivey announced that Bad Boy Mowers, a company from Batesville, Arkansas, will invest $10.5 million to open a tractor assembly plant in Monroeville, Alabama. The plant will be located in the former Vanity Fair distribution center. It is expected to create 50 jobs in the area. Governor Ivey said the project will help Monroe County and rural Alabama by supporting local employment and economic activity.
Work to prepare the site has started, according to Mike Colquett, executive director of the Monroeville/Monroe County Economic Development Authority. Colquett said Bad Boy Mowers is a good match for Monroeville. The plant will produce several tractor models, with an estimated annual output of about 9,000 units.
Ellen McNair, secretary of the Alabama Department of Commerce, said the expansion shows the company’s confidence in Alabama’s rural workforce. She noted the state’s support for business growth. Bad Boy Mowers, founded in 2002, first made zero-turn mowers and now also makes tractors, handheld tools, and UTVs.
The company was recently named Tractor Supply Co.’s top vendor for 2025, recognized for its value and supply chain solutions. Brenda Tuck, rural development manager for the Alabama Department of Commerce, said the new plant highlights the benefits of rural Alabama, including a skilled workforce and community support.
